title: IRS applies AI and machine learning to select large partnerships for examination (IR-2023–166, 8 September 2023); two AI models prioritize partnership audits
summary: IRS (8 September 2023): AI to help detect cheating and select cases; exams planned for 75 partnerships averaging over $10bn in assets. GAO (Jun 2024): two AI models prioritize partnership audits.
account: On 8 September 2023 the Internal Revenue Service (IRS) announced (IR-2023–166) a compliance effort funded by the Inflation Reduction Act. It would use improved technology and artificial intelligence to help compliance teams detect tax cheating, identify emerging compliance threats and improve case-selection tools. It described data scientists and tax-enforcement experts collaborating to apply machine learning to compliance risk in partnership, income and international tax. It planned to open examinations of 75 of the largest US partnerships, each averaging more than $10 billion in assets. These fall under the expanded Large Partnership Compliance program launched in 2021. A US Government Accountability Office (GAO) WatchBlog post of 6 June 2024 adds detail. The IRS already uses AI models to select a representative sample of returns for its annual audits. It uses two AI models to prioritize partnership returns for audit. It is piloting a new model for refundable-credit audits that IRS officials said finds risky taxpayers more effectively than the previous model. GAO recommended documenting the models and noted design weaknesses that may limit their ability to identify the highest-risk returns objectively. No cited source attributes a recovered amount to the AI selection.
purpose: Built to select high-risk returns for examination and to detect compliance threats. The claimed benefit is that purpose, with no attributable outcome documented.
system: IRS AI and machine-learning case-selection models (two partnership prioritization models; a refundable-credit audit selection model in pilot; machine learning for partnership, income and international tax risk)
model_version: TY 2021 LPC model (Large Partnership Compliance return selection model)
developer: Internal Revenue Service (in-house data scientists with tax-enforcement experts)
taxonomy_note: The good is audit case selection for the agency, and no recovered amount is attributed to AI in the sources.

ratings.reason: The IRS gives no results from the AI-selected examinations and GAO reports only officials' pilot claims.

ai_role.statement: The models prioritize or select returns for human examiners. Examinations and any assessments are human decisions. The IRS release is the deployer's own account of a system it builds in-house. The GAO post is an independent government source that relays IRS officials' claims about the pilot model and adds caveats. Neither reports an outcome attributable to the AI.

later.note: TIGTA's May 2025 audit found the Large Partnership Compliance model still in production, with the first 82 high-risk TY 2021 returns under examination, no closed examination results yet, and uncertainty over reduced staffing after the end of the contractor's work.
